title: Point Nepean Portsea Market
summary: Bi-monthly artisan market threaded through the historic Quarantine Station buildings and tea trees at Point Nepean. Make-or-grow rule for every stall, food vans, live music, roads closed to traffic.
venueName: Point Nepean National Park (Quarantine Station precinct)
priceRange: Free entry; National Park day-use fees may apply
recurrenceNote: Selected dates only – irregular (check website for future dates)
suitableFor: Families; history buffs; artisan shoppers; tourists
accessibilityNotes: Gravel/grass/bitumen paths; uneven terrain; caution with prams and wheelchairs; roads closed to traffic during market
nearbyAttractions: Fort Nepean; Point Nepean National Park walks; Portsea Hotel
suggestedItineraryPairing: Market + Fort Nepean walk + Portsea pub
editorVerdict: The setting alone earns the drive. Tea trees, old Quarantine Station buildings, and a strict make-or-grow rule that keeps the stalls honest.
editorNote:
Point Nepean Portsea Market only runs a handful of times a year inside the Quarantine Station precinct, which is exactly what makes it worth circling. Roads close to traffic, the historic buildings become a backdrop, and every stall is bound by a make-or-grow-it rule (no resellers).

Go early, the carpark fills fast and shade is genuinely limited. Pair it with a Fort Nepean walk or the cliff loop to make a day of it, and finish at the Portsea Hotel for a wine on the lawn.

Keep an eye on the Shire markets page for the next date; the schedule is seasonal and irregular. Service dogs only, no general pets.
